NAM.1.1.text: This is the burden against Nineveh, the book of the vision of Nahum the Elkoshite:

NAM.1.2.text: The LORD is a jealous and avenging God;
the LORD is avenging and full of wrath.
The LORD takes vengeance on His foes
and reserves wrath for His enemies.

NAM.1.3.text: The LORD is slow to anger
the LORD will by no means
His path is in the whirlwind and storm,
and clouds are the dust beneath His feet.

NAM.1.4.text: He rebukes the sea and dries it up;
He makes all the rivers run dry.
and the flower of Lebanon wilts.

NAM.1.5.text: the earth trembles at His presence—
the world and all its dwellers.

NAM.1.6.text: Who can endure His burning anger?
His wrath is poured out like fire;
even rocks are shattered before Him.

NAM.1.7.text: a stronghold in the day of distress;
He cares for those who trust in Him.

NAM.1.8.text: He will make an end of Nineveh
and pursue His enemies into darkness.

NAM.1.9.text: Whatever you plot against the LORD,
He will bring to an end.

NAM.1.10.text: For they will be entangled as with thorns
and consumed like the drink of a drunkard—
like stubble that is fully dry.

NAM.1.11.text: From you, O Nineveh, comes forth
a plotter of evil against the LORD,

NAM.1.12.text: This is what the LORD says:
yet they will be cut down and pass away.
Though I have afflicted you, O Judah,
I will afflict you no longer.

NAM.1.13.text: For I will now break their yoke from your neck

NAM.1.14.text: The LORD has issued a command concerning you, O Nineveh:
I will cut off the carved image and cast idol
from the house of your gods;

NAM.1.15.text: the feet of one who brings good news,
For the wicked will never again march through you;
they will be utterly cut off.

NAM.2.2.text: For the LORD will restore the splendor of Jacob
though destroyers have laid them waste
and ruined the branches of their vine.

NAM.2.3.text: The shields of his mighty men are red;
the valiant warriors are dressed in scarlet.
The fittings of the chariots flash like fire
on the day they are prepared,

NAM.2.4.text: The chariots dash through the streets;

NAM.2.5.text: the protective shield is set in place.

NAM.2.6.text: The river gates are thrown open

NAM.2.7.text: It is decreed that the city be exiled

NAM.2.8.text: Nineveh has been like a pool of water
but now it is draining away.

NAM.2.9.text: There is no end to the treasure,
an abundance of every precious thing.

NAM.2.10.text: Yes, she is desolate and laid waste!
bodies tremble, and every face grows pale!

NAM.2.11.text: or the feeding ground of the young lions,
where the lion and lioness prowled with their cubs,
with nothing to frighten them away?

NAM.2.12.text: The lion mauled enough for its cubs
and strangled prey for the lioness.
It filled its dens with the kill,
and its lairs with mauled prey.

NAM.2.13.text: “I will send your chariots up in smoke,
and the sword will devour your young lions.
I will cut off your prey from the earth,
and the voices of your messengers

NAM.3.4.text: because of the many harlotries of the harlot,
who betrays nations by her prostitution

NAM.3.5.text: “I will lift your skirts over your face.
I will show your nakedness to the nations
and your shame to the kingdoms.

NAM.3.6.text: I will pelt you with filth
I will make a spectacle of you.

NAM.3.7.text: will recoil from you and say,

NAM.3.8.text: stationed by the Nile with water around her,

NAM.3.9.text: Cush and Egypt were her boundless strength;
Put and Libya were her allies.

NAM.3.10.text: Her infants were dashed to pieces
at the head of every street.
They cast lots for her dignitaries,
and all her nobles were bound in chains.

NAM.3.11.text: and seek refuge from the enemy.

NAM.3.12.text: All your fortresses are fig trees
into the mouth of the eater!

NAM.3.13.text: are wide open to your enemies;

NAM.3.14.text: Draw your water for the siege;
Work the clay and tread the mortar;

NAM.3.15.text: There the fire will devour you;
the sword will cut you down
and consume you like a young locust.
Make yourself many like the young locust;
make yourself many like the swarming locust!

NAM.3.16.text: more than the stars of the sky.
The young locust strips the land

NAM.3.17.text: Your guards are like the swarming locust,
and your scribes like clouds of locusts
that settle on the walls on a cold day.
When the sun rises, they fly away,

NAM.3.18.text: O king of Assyria, your shepherds slumber;
Your people are scattered on the mountains
with no one to gather them.
